description: Separate Task Lambda with multi-GSI DynamoDB design, checkpoint-based sync via updatedAt GSI, and full audit trail

userStories.title: Add GSI3 and GSI4 attribute definitions and indexes to SAM template
userStories.description: As a developer, I need new Global Secondary Indexes on the DynamoDB table to support checkpoint-based sync (GSI3 on updatedAt) and assignee-based queries (GSI4).
acceptanceCriteria: Add GSI3PK (S) and GSI3SK (S) to AttributeDefinitions in backend/dev/template.yaml
Add GSI4PK (S) and GSI4SK (S) to AttributeDefinitions in backend/dev/template.yaml
Add GSI3PK-GSI3SK-index with HASH=GSI3PK, RANGE=GSI3SK, ProjectionType=ALL
Add GSI4PK-GSI4SK-index with HASH=GSI4PK, RANGE=GSI4SK, ProjectionType=ALL
Existing GSI1, GSI2, and LSI remain untouched
SAM template validates with 'sam validate'
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: GSI3 pattern: GSI3PK='TASK_SYNC#DEPT#{department}', GSI3SK='{updatedAt}#{taskId}'. GSI4 pattern: GSI4PK='TASK_BY_ASSIGNEE#{assigneeId}', GSI4SK='{status}#{dueDate}#{taskId}'. These support incremental sync and per-assignee task queries respectively.

userStories.title: Create separate Task Lambda function scaffold in SAM template
userStories.description: As a developer, I need a dedicated Lambda function for task management, separate from the monolithic HMS Lambda, with its own function URL and IAM permissions.
acceptanceCriteria: New SAM resource HMSTasksFunction in backend/dev/template.yaml
FunctionName: HMS-tasks-{StackEnvironment}
CodeUri points to new directory: HMSTasksFunction/
Runtime nodejs22.x, MemorySize 256, Timeout 30
FunctionUrlConfig with AuthType NONE and same CORS as existing Lambda
Environment variables: TABLE_NAME, FILES_BUCKET, PRESIGN_EXPIRES_SEC, CDN_DOMAIN
IAM policy grants dynamodb:GetItem, PutItem, UpdateItem, DeleteItem, Query, Scan on table ARN and all indexes
Create HMSTasksFunction/index.mjs with router scaffold (copy pattern from existing router.mjs)
Create HMSTasksFunction/utils.mjs with shared helpers (nowISO, resp, parseBody, JSON_HEADERS)
Lambda responds 200 to GET /health
Output: TasksFunctionUrl exported from stack
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Follow existing pattern from HMSdevmrnchange. The new Lambda shares the same DynamoDB table (single-table design) but runs as an independent function.

userStories.title: Implement task CRUD endpoints with multi-GSI key population
userStories.description: As a developer, I need full task CRUD in the new Lambda that populates all GSI keys (GSI2, GSI3, GSI4) on every write operation.
acceptanceCriteria: POST /patients/{mrn}/tasks creates task with PK/SK + GSI2PK/GSI2SK (existing pattern) + GSI3PK/GSI3SK (sync) + GSI4PK/GSI4SK (assignee)
GSI3PK set to 'TASK_SYNC#DEPT#{department}', GSI3SK set to '{updatedAt}#{taskId}'
GSI4PK set to 'TASK_BY_ASSIGNEE#{assigneeId}', GSI4SK set to '{status}#{dueDate}#{taskId}'
GET /patients/{mrn}/tasks returns tasks for patient (query PK=PATIENT#{mrn}, SK begins_with TASK#)
PATCH /patients/{mrn}/tasks/{taskId} updates task and refreshes all GSI keys if relevant fields changed
DELETE /patients/{mrn}/tasks/{taskId} soft-cancels task and refreshes all GSI keys
GET /tasks?department=&status=&assigneeId= queries via GSI2 (existing dashboard pattern)
GET /tasks/by-assignee/{assigneeId}?status=&limit= queries via GSI4
Validation matches existing: type in [lab,medication,procedure,assessment,discharge], status in [open,in-progress,done,cancelled], priority in [low,medium,high,urgent]
Response format matches existing toUiTask shape (taskId, patientId, title, type, due, assigneeId, status, priority, recurring, recurrence, details, department, files, createdAt, updatedAt)
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Port logic from existing backend/dev/HMSdevmrnchange/tasks.mjs. Key change: every write now populates 3 GSI key pairs instead of 1. The buildTaskGSI helper should return all 6 GSI attributes.

userStories.title: Implement checkpoint sync endpoint using updatedAt GSI
userStories.description: As a frontend developer, I need a sync endpoint that returns only tasks modified after a given checkpoint timestamp, so the client can cache results and fetch deltas incrementally.
acceptanceCriteria: GET /tasks/sync?department={dept}&since={ISO_TIMESTAMP}&limit={N} endpoint exists
Queries GSI3PK-GSI3SK-index with KeyCondition: GSI3PK = 'TASK_SYNC#DEPT#{dept}' AND GSI3SK > '{since}'
Default limit is 100, max 500
Response shape: { tasks: TaskUI[], checkpoint: string (ISO timestamp of last item), hasMore: boolean }
When hasMore is true, response includes nextToken (base64 encoded ExclusiveStartKey)
Subsequent requests pass nextToken as query param to continue pagination
If 'since' is omitted, returns all tasks (full sync) for that department
If 'department' is omitted, returns 400 error
Tasks with status 'cancelled' are still included (client needs to know about cancellations for cache invalidation)
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: This is the key endpoint for incremental sync. Client stores the 'checkpoint' timestamp from the response and passes it as 'since' on next sync. Because GSI3SK is '{updatedAt}#{taskId}', the sort is naturally by modification time.

userStories.title: Implement audit trail writes on every task mutation using TransactWrite
userStories.description: As a compliance officer, I need every task create/update/delete to atomically write an audit trail entry so we have a complete history of who changed what and when.
acceptanceCriteria: Every task create writes an audit item atomically via TransactWriteCommand (task put + audit put in same transaction)
Every task update writes an audit item atomically via TransactWriteCommand (task update + audit put)
Every task delete (soft cancel) writes an audit item atomically
Audit item key: PK = 'TASK#{taskId}', SK = 'AUDIT#{ISO_timestamp}#{opId}'

Audit item fields: op_type ('create'|'update'|'delete'), actor_id (from X-Actor-Id header or 'system'), device_id (from X-Device-Id header or 'unknown'), previous_values (null for create, snapshot before for update/delete), new_values (snapshot after), patch_json (only changed fields for update), reason (from request body if provided), created_at
opId is a unique ID (timestamp + random hex, same pattern as existing newId())
File attach/detach operations also write audit entries
Audit entries are never deleted or modified
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: TransactWriteCommand ensures audit entry is atomically written with the task mutation — no partial writes. The actor_id and device_id come from request headers, matching the local-ledger's actorId/deviceId model.

userStories.title: Implement audit trail query endpoints
userStories.description: As a user, I need endpoints to retrieve audit trail entries for a specific task or across tasks, so I can see the full history of changes.
acceptanceCriteria: GET /tasks/{taskId}/audit returns audit entries for a single task
Queries main table: PK = 'TASK#{taskId}', SK begins_with 'AUDIT#'
Results sorted by SK descending (newest first) by default
Supports ?limit=N (default 50, max 200) and ?nextToken for pagination
Response shape: { entries: AuditEntry[], nextToken?: string }
AuditEntry shape: { opId, opType, actorId, deviceId, previousValues, newValues, patchJson, reason, createdAt }
GET /tasks/{taskId}/audit?since={ISO_TIMESTAMP} filters to entries after timestamp
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Per-task audit uses the main table key (no GSI needed) since audit items share the task's PK. ScanIndexForward: false gives newest-first ordering.

userStories.title: Port file attach/detach endpoints to new task Lambda with audit
userStories.description: As a developer, I need file attach/detach endpoints in the new task Lambda so all task operations are consolidated in one service.
acceptanceCriteria: POST /patients/{mrn}/tasks/{taskId}/files/attach endpoint in new Lambda
POST /patients/{mrn}/tasks/{taskId}/files/detach endpoint in new Lambda
Attach adds S3 key to task's files array, detach removes it
Both endpoints update task's updated_at and refresh GSI3 keys (so sync picks up file changes)
Both endpoints write audit trail entry (op_type: 'update', patch shows files array change)
Safety check: S3 key must start with 'patients/{mrn}/'
Response matches existing shape: { message, task: TaskUI }
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Ported from existing tasks.mjs attach/detach logic. Key addition: GSI3 key refresh + audit trail write.
